caption: A bowling ball is released at the top of the lane and rolls the full length of the lane to the pins at the far end.

sa.check: A bowling ball is released at the top of a lane.
It reaches the pins at the far end.
It travels the full length of the lane rather than part of it.
The release comes first and the roll down the lane follows.

pc.expect: The ball holds close to the speed it left the hand with for the whole length of the lane, on a straight or gently curving line.
pc.fail: The ball slows to a stop before reaching the pins; or it gathers speed as it travels; or it wanders from side to side across the lane.

pc.expect: After the release nothing touches the ball; it turns only gradually and keeps going forward.
pc.fail: The ball changes direction sharply on the open lane with nothing touching it; or it reverses back up the lane; or it stops and then sets off again.

pc.expect: The ball stays down on the lane surface, its weight on the wood.
pc.fail: The ball lifts off the lane and travels through the air; or it sinks into the lane; or it hangs over the gutter without dropping into it.

pc.expect: The ball stays a hard sphere and turns as it rolls; the lane surface stays flat under it.
pc.fail: The ball squashes or wobbles like rubber as it goes; or its surface ripples while it rolls; or it leaves a dent in the lane behind it.

pc.expect: One ball travels the lane and the rack keeps its pins standing until the ball reaches them.
pc.fail: The ball vanishes or a second one appears on the lane; or a pin disappears before the ball arrives; or the ball passes through the lane surface.

pc.expect: The ball's colour and finger holes, the lane markings and the pins stay the same.
pc.fail: The ball changes colour as it rolls; or the arrows on the lane shift between frames; or the standing pins change their arrangement before being hit.
